references.text: Psalm 107:20 says that God sent his word and healed them. The officer believes that Jesus can heal with just a word, just as God heals by his word.
The parallel passage in Matthew 8:8 recounts the same event where the officer says to Jesus: "Say only a word, and my servant will be healed."
In Matthew 8:13, Jesus heals the officer's servant at a distance with just a word, confirming the officer's faith that Jesus' word alone was sufficient.
In John 4:49–50, Jesus heals a royal official's son at a distance simply by saying a word, paralleling the officer's faith that Jesus could heal without being physically present.

The previous verse (Luke 7:6) explains why the officer did not consider himself worthy for Jesus to come under his roof, providing context for why he also did not consider himself worthy to approach Jesus directly.
Psalm 33:9 says that the Lord spoke, and it happened. The officer's faith that Jesus' word alone is sufficient reflects this understanding of the power of God's word.
In Luke 7:9, Jesus expresses admiration for the officer's great faith—a faith demonstrated precisely in his conviction that Jesus could heal with just a word.
Moses asked God to heal Miriam with a simple prayer. The officer's plea for healing through Jesus' word alone parallels this trust in God's healing word.
